READABILITY.evidence: Very large single main.zig file (~133KB). It uses single-letter/cryptic names in kernel logic (Y1, Y2, U, V, lf, cf, s16, u8_v) and unexplained magic shuffle constants (24294, 48001, -22049, 19780) without comments mapping them to FFmpeg.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: One src/main.zig of about 133KB. Process functions are monolithic, with deep nesting (for/switch inside while inside if inside loops). yuvToRgbPair switch arms are copy-pasted per format. .zig-cache and zig-out binaries were committed.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Many magic constants (1 << 18, >> 19, 144, 190, 165, mulhi coefficients) with no named constants. Clamping exists, but there is little visible input validation. 'else => unreachable' is used in dispatch paths.

C8-02-CASE1.evidence: Hidden correctness test failed. The final run shows 57/58 within bars, and nearest-scaling rgb24 720x576->360x288 gives wrong pixels (cand differs from ref at index 6), so the scaling geometry/position logic is incorrect. SIMD loops do have scalar tails.

C8-02-CASE2.evidence: Builds libswscale_candidate.so through the scaffold build.zig, which targets x86-64-v3. The three exports appear intact, and the perf-check runs succeed in building and converting. Nothing shows extra exports being verified, and build artifacts were committed into the workspace.
